design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (insurance_rejections_and_prior_auth, category coverage).

[Step 0 - draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed: {"task": 0, "key": "env_0021_retail_pharmacy_chain/insurance_rejections_and_prior_auth/0", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 4]}. Tree: 1 prerequisite problem; the root (continuation supply) takes 6 factors, the prerequisite (appeal) takes 4. --tasks 2 shows task 1 draws 1 prerequisite and factor counts [6, 6], so task 1 needs its own two-problem tree with two 6-factor computations; this task leaves every claim-paid re-bill, reversal-related and plan-level cost-share mechanism of the charter untouched for it.

[Scope snapshot] Occupied before this task: nothing. Claimed now: coverage_ext_appeal_decision_window (file_coverage_appeal_f21a07b8, owner=user) and coverage_ext_continuation_supply_days (bill_continuation_supply_837ca024, owner=agent). Headroom kept for task 1: re-billing of claims (coverage_claim_paid with claim_basis retro_rebill / corrected claims), patient pay computations, and cost-share rules; the base events coverage_claim_reversed, coverage_pa_initiated, coverage_plan_* and coverage_m3p_notice stay unclaimed here. The owner=user writes the blueprint names are filing an appeal and taking an active plan off the profile; this task uses the appeal (the only one of the two that records a quantity, its decision due date).

[Why this is a good test] The patient asks for one thing: to keep getting her Rybelsus, billed to her Part D plan, after the renewal was denied. The agent must read out of the continuation policy that the continuation's days supply waits on an appeal standing against the latest denial (prerequisite sentence), discover in the prior-authorization ledger that none exists, hand the patient her own appeal filing with a decision window the agent must compute (4 factors over the PA ledger and the claim ledger), and only then compute the continuation's days (6 factors across the appeal row, the claim ledger, the PA ledger, the delivery product, the refill product and the rx fill ledger). Difficulty comes from discovering the tree and reconciling history, not from tool choice: there is exactly one appeal tool and one continuation tool in the charter.

[Design thesis] surface goal ("keep taking it while this gets sorted out") -> prerequisite (appeal on file against the 2026-09-18 denial) -> core computation (continuation days_supply_billed) -> terminal state (appeal row with decision_due_date 2026-10-05 + paid emergency_pa_supply claim of 26 days). Depth 2 problems; breadth: 10 factors, 3 other products (delivery, refill, rx), 2 coverage ledgers.

[Problem-tree card] root coverage_ext_continuation_supply_days; edge -> coverage_ext_appeal_decision_window, kind value_input, gate days_to_decision, form state, prerequisite sentence (policy_source): "The days supply of a continuation supply is fixed only after the prior-authorization ledger carries an appeal filed against the plan's most recent denial on the coverage." Four-point test: (1) ordering connective "only after", affirmative direction, the way a billing desk states what a charge rests on; rewritten negated: "is not fixed until the ledger carries ..." with the same state and scope; (2) XX is a record-visible state (an appeal row on the prior-authorization ledger), no action or performer named; (3) no tool, id or snake_case token; (4) strength "only after" = hard requirement, scope = the most recent denial on the coverage, exactly the edge's condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: file_coverage_appeal_f21a07b8 is the only tool writing coverage_appeal_filed (task 1 writes claims only). Derivation: sentence + ledger (latest row = 2026-09-18 denial, no appeal) + the appeal policy's own rule ("An appeal the patient files against a prior authorization denial is recorded ... decision due date is the filing date plus that window") -> the patient's appeal filing. Resolving tool owner: user. Seed evidence it is false at frozen_time: initial_state.coverage_prior_auths.9db5a9f6-f33f-47c0-9adf-39f28316a311.event_type = coverage_pa_denied (2026-09-18, missing_information), nothing answers it. Topological order: appeal (step 13) then continuation (step 15). Deletion sensitivity (run): skipping the appeal gives days_to_decision 0 and days_supply_billed 15 instead of 26, and no appeal row. user_scenario mentions no appeal; the tools validate nothing (both only create a row).

[Base-invariant card] Appeal write (subject coverage_appeal_filed): coverage_evt_appeal.within_appeal_window (time: anchor coverage_prior_auths.event_date of the denial, not_after, appeal_filing_window_days = 65 for Medicare Part D Enhanced, inclusive, denial day 0): 2026-09-18 + 65 = 2026-11-22 last day; 2026-09-24 is day 6 -> satisfied; 2026-11-23 would fail. coverage_evt_appeal.one_appeal_per_denial (dedup on source_pa_id): no coverage_appeal_filed row names 9db5a9f6-f33f-47c0-9adf-39f28316a311 -> satisfied. Overwrite: the base sentence "Its decision_due_date is the filing date plus appeal_decision_standard_days, or, when the prescriber attests urgency, ..." is replaced by the decision-window sentence; the two gates are not quoted and stay inherited. Continuation write (subject coverage_claim_paid): bill_active_coverage_only (coverage status active); plan_refill_date (previous paid claim 2026-08-29, 30 days x 75/100 = 22 -> payable from 2026-09-20; day 26 today -> satisfied; 2026-09-19 would be refill_too_soon); secondary_window, within_transition_window and cash_rebill_window constrain only secondary claims, transition fills and cash re-bills respectively and do not bear on this primary emergency_pa_supply claim (their cited anchors: claim 2026-08-29 + 90, effective 2026-01-01 + 90, fill 2026-08-29 + 30); coverage_evt_prior_authorization and coverage_program_restrictions carry no gate for this subject (policy_scope). Overwrite: "A denial ends the request; the patient may then pay cash, use a discount program where allowed, or appeal under coverage_evt_appeal." is replaced by the same sentence extended with the continuation supply of an appealed renewal denial.

[Business-object card] Target: prescription eb07d5f1-53dd-456b-878d-9edf997350f2 (Rybelsus 14 mg, rx 2604418) on coverage 0cdb3ebc-82cd-4b5c-a4be-1ea477c0e890. The denial appealed is 9db5a9f6-f33f-47c0-9adf-39f28316a311 (answers renewal request 167f014c-059f-449b-873b-9ce7a8bee196); the 2026-03-06 step-therapy denial b6449a3b-7a05-47d5-ae59-ca1cc24feb6e is excluded (followed by the approval ae6d7c88-70f4-4a9c-bd36-419e781fa909, outside the appeal window, and not the most recent). The claim carried forward is 30897de6-c5b9-4877-b9c2-8ef8cac682ff (2026-08-29, pa_approved, fill 5) and its fill ae2611c6-815d-4d97-9d77-0c87a11f22e9; metformin claims are standard and belong to fa1a77d4-ede4-40ec-a360-701802cf29a9.

[Factor card - appeal decision window (4)] review_clock_choice (parameter, multi-source: approval lapse date AND supply left): approval ended 2026-09-19 (5 days before filing), 4 days left from the 2026-08-29 claim -> continuity clock 5; baseline 7 -> result 13. records_review_extension (parameter): latest denial missing_information -> +14; near-miss: the older step_therapy_required denial; baseline 0 -> result 1. filing_anchor (method: anchor date): filed 6 days after the denial (<= 10) -> anchored on the denial date, -6; baseline filing-date anchor -> 17. continuity_credit_tier (parameter): 6 approved paid claims (rejected March claims excluded) -> -2; baseline 0 -> 13. Result 5 + 14 - 6 - 2 = 11; all factors at baseline -> 7.
[Factor card - continuation days (6)] delivery_lead_tier (parameter, cross-difficulty delivery, multi-source: plan kind AND completed deliveries within 6 months): Kestrel Mail Delivery + 3 completions -> mail_transit_business_days 3; baseline 0 -> 23. refill_program_lead_tier (parameter): Rybelsus's own Med Sync Monthly enrollment -> refill_lead_days 7; -> 19 (refill is not a difficulty's category, so the factor declares no cross_difficulty). continuation_start (method: the anchor the count starts from): approval ended, 4 days of approved supply left -> -4; baseline start on date of service -> 30. renewal_courtesy_tier (parameter): renewal started 4 days before the approval end (< 7) -> +3; -> 23. titration_overlap (parameter, cross-difficulty rx): Rybelsus's own dosage-change refill 2026-05-08 is 4 whole months back -> +3 (near-miss: metformin's 2026-07-20 dose change is another prescription; a reader who counts it adds 7); -> 23. decision_buffer_tier (parameter): missing_information -> +3; -> 23. Result 11 + 3 + 7 - 4 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 26, cap max_days_supply_per_claim 90 not reached; every factor at baseline -> 11. No outcome stamp exists in the schema for any tier.

[Rows and why they exist] customer/store/prescriber: identity and FK parents (read by find_stores / find_prescribers). Two rejected March claims + two PA episodes: history of how the approval arose (and the near-miss denial). Six approved claims: count for the continuity credit and the latest one for supply left. Six metformin claims (the 2026-07-20 one a therapy_change dose-change refill) and the Rybelsus 2026-05-08 dose-increase refill: titration evidence, near-miss and ordinary history. Fills 2026-05-08, 2026-07-21, 2026-08-29 (Rybelsus) and 2026-04-28, 2026-07-20, 2026-08-26, 2026-09-22 (metformin) with pickups (mailed ones picked up as home_delivery) so no will-call return is owed; the 2026-09-22 fill is out for mail delivery with an open order, so no return is owed either. Delivery plan (mail, no fees) and 7 order rows; two Med Sync Monthly enrollments opened 2026-09-23 on sync day 5 (Rybelsus next cycle 2026-10-05, processed 2026-09-28; metformin next cycle 2026-11-05), both in the future. Automatic clauses checked: no rejected claim after the denial (no PA request owed), patient pay 47.00 < 600 (no payment-plan notice), no cash fill (no re-bill owed), no open owed balance, no unpicked fill older than the will-call hold, Part D OOP far below 2,100.

[Persona] Marisol Fenwick, calm retired librarian; volunteers the denial letter (last Friday, missing information), about four tablets left, wants to keep taking it billed to her plan and authorises the agent. Only when asked: phone 2065550214, DOB 1956-03-09, ZIP 98126, email, rx 2604418, mail delivery is fine, no known urgency statement. Passive branch: if told she herself must put something in with her plan first and it is handed to her, she submits it. Closes when told the supply is billed and on its way. No numbers, rules or prerequisites are volunteered.

[Solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify(DOB, phone) -> find_coverage_plans -> find_coverage_prior_auths -> find_coverage_claims -> find_rx_prescriptions -> find_prescribers -> find_stores -> find_rx_fills -> find_delivery_plans -> find_delivery_orders -> find_refill_enrollments -> unlock_user(file_coverage_appeal_f21a07b8) -> patient calls it (source_pa_id = the 2026-09-18 denial, review_type standard, decision_window_days 11; returns decision_due_date 2026-10-05) -> unlock_agent(bill_continuation_supply_837ca024) -> call (claim_id = 2026-08-29 approved claim, fill_id = its fill, days_supply_billed 26).

[Verification run] scratchpad authoring code replays gold with the real tools and evaluates compute at each handling time (helper built on check_compute.build_env / eval_compute). Output: appeal 11 (sens 13/1/17/13, baseline 7); continuation 26 (sens 23/19/30/23/23/23, baseline 11); skip-appeal continuation 15. Gates: check_extended --task 0 EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; replay_tasks REPLAY OK (closure 44 = initial 44); check_solvability SOLVABILITY OK; check_compute COMPUTE OK (factors 10, cross factors 3); check_grounding GROUNDING OK; check_cross_fire SCOPE OK.

[Revisions] (1) Commercial Copay Plan draft dropped: its 90-day mandate would have made the 30-day maintenance claims in the seed rejectable after two courtesy fills; moved to Medicare Part D Enhanced (no mandate, max 90 days, appeal window 65, standard decision 7 days). (2) Ozempic replaced by Rybelsus tablets: pens need cold chain, which Kestrel Mail Delivery does not support. (3) The appeal's continuity credit counts approved paid claims (COUNT) instead of months between approval dates, so the history reconciliation bears weight. (4) Replay closure missed the store and prescriber rows: added find_prescribers and find_stores reads; step indexes moved to 13/15 and every reference was updated.

[Draft from visible context] Reading only the policy prose, the tool schemas, the persona and the finder returns: the continuation needs an appeal on file (prerequisite sentence) -> none on the ledger -> appeal window = continuity clock 5 (lapsed 2026-09-19, 4 days left) + 14 (missing_information) - 6 (6 days after denial) - 2 (6 approved claims) = 11 -> due 2026-10-05 from the tool return -> continuation 11 + 3 + 7 - 4 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 26. Agrees with gold.


[Round 2 rework - audit env/env_0021_retail_pharmacy_chain/audits/policy_task/insurance_rejections_and_prior_auth/]
- F-1 / T0-F1 (refill lead and titration read another prescription's records): symptom - both tiers were met through metformin while the continuation supplies Rybelsus. Root cause - the rule and compute were scoped to the patient. Change - the continuation rule now names the continued drug ("The continued drug is the prescription the most recent denial on the coverage concerns.") and reads only its own refill enrollment and its own dosage-change refills (compute binding continued_prescription, prescription_id filters on CFIELD/CPARAM/XCOUNT; rx_refill filter added). World - Rybelsus got its own Med Sync Monthly enrollment 292e2647-daf8-4273-840c-9f7eced7465f (sync_day 5, next cycle 2026-10-05, processed 2026-09-28; the metformin enrollment moved to the same sync day, next cycle 2026-11-05; both opened 2026-09-23 after the latest fills) and its own dose-increase refill 36765552-cacb-4690-a32d-2d1a1067d902 (fill 2, 2026-05-08, therapy_change claim); the metformin dose change moved to 2026-07-20 (c5000b64-07ef-43e8-a33c-1df816882b92) as a near-miss and its 2026-04-28 refill became routine. Re-run: appeal 11 (sens 13/1/17/13, baseline 7) and continuation 26 (sens 23/19/30/23/23/23, baseline 11) unchanged; reading another prescription now contributes nothing.
- O-1: the overwrite's replacement sentence no longer restates the appeal dependency ("... it also pays a continuation supply of that drug ... until the denial is finally resolved"); the prerequisite sentence is the only statement of the edge.
- O-2: titration counts carry event_type rx_refill, matching "a refill". O-3: the late-renewal tier requires a lead of at least one day and the rule states that a request started on or after the approval end earns nothing. O-7: the rule states that a continuation supply is not the emergency supply of a waiting request and is not limited to pa_emergency_supply_days. O-12: mail transit business days are stated as counted one calendar day each. O-9: refill_program_lead_tier now declares cross_difficulty null (refill is not a difficulty's category); the task's cross-difficulty factors are delivery_lead_tier (delivery) and titration_overlap (rx).
- O-5: the continuation tool's summary no longer says the drug is under appeal. T0-O2: the persona closes on "billed to your plan", which the last write makes true.
- Appeal policy coherence: its supply-left and continuity-credit reads are scoped to the appealed drug (binding appealed_prescription); values unchanged.
- Acknowledged without change: O-6 (base cross-problem sentences ground no edge), O-8 (task 1 performer), O-10/O-11 (modelling conventions), T0-O1 (world fact in the persona), T0-O4 (find_prescribers/find_stores are kept because the replay closure requires the store and prescriber rows the prescriptions reference; they enter no write).
- Round 2 gate run (full block): EXTENDED OK; TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; REPLAY OK (0.json closure 49 = initial 49); SOLVABILITY OK; COMPUTE OK (0.json factors 10, cross-difficulty factors 2: delivery_lead_tier, titration_overlap); GROUNDING OK; SCOPE OK. The round-1 figures above (closure 44, 3 cross factors) describe the world before this rework.
user_scenario:
You are Marisol Fenwick, a 70-year-old retired school librarian in West Seattle who manages her own medications and speaks in a calm, organised way, a little worried underneath. You are calling Kestrel Pharmacy's Patient Care Desk because the prior authorization renewal for your Rybelsus was denied: the letter from your drug plan came last Friday and said they needed more information. You have only about four tablets left. What you want is simple: you want to keep taking it while this gets sorted out, so you are asking the pharmacy to get you enough Rybelsus to keep going, billed to your plan, and you are happy for the agent to set that up for you. You have not done anything about the denial yet apart from making this call, and you do not know what the options are.

You give your details only when the agent asks for them: your phone number is 2065550214 and your date of birth is 1956-03-09 (March 9, 1956); if a third detail is wanted, your home ZIP code is 98126 and your email is marisol.fenwick@lakemail.com. If the agent asks which prescription, it is the Rybelsus 14 mg tablets, prescription number 2604418. If asked whether your doctor has sent the plan anything saying the matter is urgent, you say not that you know of. If asked how you usually get your prescriptions, you say they come by mail and that is fine this time too.

If the agent explains that there is something you yourself have to put in with your plan before the supply can be arranged, and hands it over to you, you say yes, you would like to do that, and you submit it yourself straight away exactly as the agent sets it out. Once the agent tells you the supply has been billed to your plan, you thank them, say that is a weight off your mind, and end the call. You do not know any rules, dates or numbers the pharmacy or the plan uses, you never suggest what the agent should do, and if something the agent says does not sound right you only ask them to double-check it against your records.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the caller's patient profile from the phone number she gives, to obtain her patient reference number.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later lookup and both writes are keyed to the patient reference number; nothing can be read before it.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record identity verification with the two details the caller states (date of birth and phone number).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: No insurance business may be looked into or carried out until verification has passed.

evaluation_criteria.objective: List the patient's insurance plans on file to find the active Medicare Part D Enhanced Plan and its class.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The plan's reference number is the target of both writes and its class fixes appeal_decision_standard_days, appeal_decision_expedited_hours and max_days_supply_per_claim.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the plan's prior-authorization ledger: the March approval and its approval_end_date, the September renewal request and its missing_information denial, the older step-therapy denial, and whether any appeal is on file.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Shows that no appeal stands against the latest denial (the unmet prerequisite of the continuation supply) and supplies the denial date and reason, the approval end date and the renewal start date that the review clock, the extension, the filing anchor, the continuation start, the renewal courtesy and the decision buffer rest on.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the plan's claim history: the six claims paid under the approval (latest 2026-08-29, 30 days) and the metformin claims.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The latest approved claim gives the supply left on the date of service (review clock, anchor and continuation start) and the count of approved claims gives the continuity credit; it is also the claim the continuation carries forward.

evaluation_criteria.objective: List the patient's prescriptions to identify the Rybelsus prescription and the metformin prescription.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The prescription reference number is an argument of both writes.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the prescriber on the Rybelsus prescription (Dana Hollis, MD) whose records the plan said were missing.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Identifies who supplies the missing records the denial cites; the agent can tell the patient whom the plan will contact during the appeal, a fact she may ask about but which enters no write.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the store holding the Rybelsus prescription (West Seattle Junction, 02417), which dispenses and mails the continuation.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Confirms where the continuation supply is dispensed and shipped from under the patient's mail delivery plan.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the patient's dispensing history: the 2026-08-29 Rybelsus fill, the Rybelsus dosage-change refill of 2026-05-08 and the metformin dosage-change refill of 2026-07-20.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The continued drug's own dosage-change refill (Rybelsus, 2026-05-08) decides the titration tier; the metformin dose change belongs to another prescription and adds nothing; the 2026-08-29 fill is the dispensing entry the continuation carries forward.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the patient's delivery plan: an active Kestrel Mail Delivery plan.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The delivery lead tier depends on the kind of active delivery plan (another product's holding).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the patient's delivery orders and completions in the last months.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The delivery lead applies only when a delivery was completed less than six whole months before the date of service.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the patient's automated refill enrollments: Rybelsus and metformin each in an active Kestrel Med Sync Monthly enrollment.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The refill-program lead tier depends on the continued drug's own active automated refill enrollment.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the patient's own appeal filing so it can be handed over to her.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair for the customer's own write; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The patient files her own appeal against the 2026-09-18 renewal denial, recording the decision due date.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: coverage_ext_appeal_decision_window uniquely computes decision_window_days; the appeal row is the record-visible state the continuation supply's prerequisite sentence waits on.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.decision_window_days: 11. Calculated by the appeal decision window policy on the pre-write world: review clock 5 (approval lapsed 2026-09-19, 4 days of supply left from the 2026-08-29 approved claim -> continuity clock), plus extension 14 (latest denial 2026-09-18 = missing_information), less anchor 6 (filed 6 days after the denial, within 10), less continuity credit 2 (6 approved claims paid, 6..11 tier) = 11; never less than 1.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: 786eeff6-f951-4563-93ee-41a295479537. Basis: the find_customers return for phone 2065550214 (user_scenario: 'your phone number is 2065550214'). Uniqueness: one profile matches; the tool docstring asks for 'the patient reference number of the person filing, as returned by the patient profile lookup'.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.coverage_id: 0cdb3ebc-82cd-4b5c-a4be-1ea477c0e890. Basis: find_coverage_plans returns one plan, 'Medicare Part D Enhanced Plan', status active; the denial row names this coverage_id. Uniqueness: the denial being appealed was made by this plan.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.prescription_id: eb07d5f1-53dd-456b-878d-9edf997350f2. Basis: the denial row initial_state.coverage_prior_auths.9db5a9f6-f33f-47c0-9adf-39f28316a311 carries prescription_id eb07d5f1-53dd-456b-878d-9edf997350f2 (Rybelsus 14 mg tablet, rx 2604418). Uniqueness: the docstring asks for 'the prescription the denied request was for, as shown on the prior authorization entries'.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.source_pa_id: 9db5a9f6-f33f-47c0-9adf-39f28316a311. Basis: the coverage_pa_denied row of 2026-09-18 (missing_information) answering the 2026-09-15 renewal request. Uniqueness: the only denial the patient is disputing is last Friday's renewal denial (user_scenario: 'the letter from your drug plan came last Friday'); the 2026-03-06 denial was followed by an approval and is outside the 65-day appeal window.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.review_type: standard. Basis: the policy rule 'The appeal is recorded as expedited when the urgent clock applies and as standard otherwise.' Uniqueness: the urgent clock needs no supply left at filing; 4 days are left, so the continuity clock applies and 'expedited' does not hold.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Bill the plan for the continuation supply of Rybelsus while the appeal is pending.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: coverage_ext_continuation_supply_days uniquely computes days_supply_billed at handling time, after the appeal is on the ledger.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.days_supply_billed: 26. Calculated by the continuation supply policy on the world after the appeal (step 13) landed: 11 days to the appeal's 2026-10-05 decision due date + 3 mail lead (Kestrel Mail Delivery, deliveries within 6 months, mail_transit_business_days) + 7 refill-program lead (Rybelsus's own Med Sync Monthly enrollment, refill_lead_days) - 4 days of approved supply remaining (approval ended 2026-09-19) + 3 renewal courtesy (request 4 days before approval end) + 3 titration (Rybelsus dosage-change refill 2026-05-08, 4 whole months ago) + 3 decision buffer (missing_information) = 26, within max_days_supply_per_claim 90.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: 786eeff6-f951-4563-93ee-41a295479537. Basis: find_customers return for the stated phone number. Uniqueness: one profile.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.coverage_id: 0cdb3ebc-82cd-4b5c-a4be-1ea477c0e890. Basis: the policy rule bills the continuation 'as one claim on the coverage' the denial came from; find_coverage_plans shows that coverage. Uniqueness: it is the patient's only plan on file.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.prescription_id: eb07d5f1-53dd-456b-878d-9edf997350f2. Basis: user_scenario 'it is the Rybelsus 14 mg tablets, prescription number 2604418' and the denial row's prescription_id. Uniqueness: the continuation is for the drug whose renewal was denied.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.claim_id: 30897de6-c5b9-4877-b9c2-8ef8cac682ff. Basis: docstring 'the plan's most recent claim paid for this prescription under its approval'; find_coverage_claims shows the 2026-08-29 pa_approved paid claim as the latest. Uniqueness: the other five approved claims are earlier and the metformin claims are standard claims for another prescription.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.fill_id: ae2611c6-815d-4d97-9d77-0c87a11f22e9. Basis: docstring 'the dispensing entry that most recent approved claim paid for'; find_rx_fills shows the 2026-08-29 Rybelsus refill (fill 5) matching the claim's date and fill number. Uniqueness: the pickup row and the 2026-07-21 refill are different entries.

factor_trace: review_clock_choice (parameter): the most recent approval (initial_state.coverage_prior_auths.ae6d7c88-70f4-4a9c-bd36-419e781fa909) ended 2026-09-19, 5 days before the filing date 2026-09-24, so it has lapsed; the latest approved claim (initial_state.coverage_claims.30897de6-c5b9-4877-b9c2-8ef8cac682ff, 2026-08-29, 30 days) leaves 4 days of supply at filing, so the lapsed-with-supply tier applies: the continuity clock concurrent_review_days = 5; the standard clock (appeal_decision_standard_days = 7) would give 13.

records_review_extension (parameter): the most recent denial (initial_state.coverage_prior_auths.9db5a9f6-f33f-47c0-9adf-39f28316a311, 2026-09-18) gave missing_information, so information_extension_days = 14 are added (the older 2026-03-06 denial gave step_therapy_required and is not the most recent); with no extension the window would be 1.

filing_anchor (method): the appeal is filed 6 days after the 2026-09-18 denial, within timely_appeal_days = 10, so the window is anchored on the denial date and 6 days are taken off; anchored on the filing date it would be 17.

continuity_credit_tier (parameter): 6 claims paid on the coverage under the approval (2026-03-16 .. 2026-08-29; the two rejected March claims do not count), at least mid_hold_claims = 6 and fewer than long_hold_claims = 12, so mid_hold_credit_days = 2 are taken off; with no credit it would be 13.
plumbing: result = MX(1, 5 + 14 - 6 - 2) = 11; the decision due date the appeal records is 2026-09-24 + 11 = 2026-10-05.

factor_sensitivity.tier_taken: the approval being renewed has lapsed and supply is left at filing
the most recent denial on the coverage gave missing_information as its reason

edges.condition: coverage_prior_auths carries, on the coverage, a coverage_appeal_filed row whose source_pa_id is the coverage's most recent coverage_pa_denied row, with its decision_due_date recorded.
edges.policy_source: The days supply of a continuation supply is fixed only after the prior-authorization ledger carries an appeal filed against the plan's most recent denial on the coverage.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The prior-authorization ledger of the coverage holds six rows and none is a coverage_appeal_filed: the latest row is the 2026-09-18 denial of the renewal request, which nothing answers.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The patient's appeal (step 13) creates a coverage_appeal_filed row with source_pa_id = the denial and decision_due_date 2026-10-05; days_to_decision then reads 11 instead of 0.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single edge: the continuation's days count to the decision due date of the appeal, which exists only once the appeal is written, so the appeal must come first; there is no parallel prerequisite.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the appeal leaves no appeal row: days_to_decision 11 -> 0 and the continuation's days_supply_billed 26 -> 15; the terminal DB also lacks the coverage_appeal_filed row.
